model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis, logarithmic scale from 1 to 10⁴) and classification accuracy (y-axis, linear scale from 35% to 65%) for six different methods: Base (black solid line with circular markers), FT (cyan solid line with triangular markers), IKE (red solid line with triangular markers), MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers), MEMIT (purple solid line with circular markers), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). As the co-occurrence number increases, most methods show a general upward trend in accuracy, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy, rising from approximately 51% at 1 to 66% at 10⁴. MEND and MEMIT also show strong growth, reaching around 56% and 55% respectively at 10⁴. FT and IKE show moderate improvement, ending near 48% and 49%. The Base method remains relatively flat, increasing only slightly from ~38% to ~44%. All lines are connected with solid lines and marked with distinct shapes corresponding to their legend entries.
